sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas restored to x^0 = c t
sources.locator: Sections 3.5.2 pp. 60-62 (acceleration vector and constant proper acceleration), 3.9.1-3.9.3 pp. 69-74 (thickening, Bell's spaceship paradox and accelerated simultaneity), 7.1 pp. 147-148 (accelerated coordinates), 8.1.1-8.1.4 pp. 165-168 (rotating frames, the Sagnac effect and rotating coordinates), 9.5.1-9.5.5 pp. 204-211 (congruences, expansion, rigidity, Herglotz-Noether in 1+1 dimensions and Bell revisited); printed page numbers as in the PDF text layer

contents.name: Section 3.5.2 pp. 61-62: the acceleration four-vector, its squared magnitude, and the acceleration measured by an accelerometer carried along the worldline
contents.support: The definition, its units and the ideal-accelerometer reading are the exact content of this item; the covariant identity eta(A,A) >= 0 is supplied by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition.

contents.name: Section 3.5.2 pp. 61-62, Example 4: constant proper acceleration with t = (1/a) sinh(a tau), x = (1/a) cosh(a tau)
contents.support: Recomputed exactly with c retained as x(tau) = (c^2/alpha)(sinh(alpha tau/c), cosh(alpha tau/c)), including the constant four-acceleration magnitude, the wedge bound and the identification as a Rindler flow line.

contents.name: Section 3.5.2 p. 62: the lightlike asymptote of hyperbolic motion and the resulting event horizon
contents.support: The asymptotic approach to the null planes is proved as clause (i) of the theorem and the causal horizon criteria as clause (ii).

contents.name: Sections 3.9.1-3.9.2 pp. 69-72: the thickening picture, Bell's spaceship paradox with equal launch-frame accelerations, and the thread stretched relative to its unstressed length and under tension
contents.support: The thought experiment retains the kinematic core (constant chart separation, nonzero longitudinal expansion, growing rest separation) and marks the tension/breaking reading as conditional on an elasticity model, which the source's prose does not provide.

contents.name: Section 3.9.3 pp. 73-74: local failure of simultaneity for accelerated observers
contents.reason: The accelerated-simultaneity discussion and its worked rotating-frame holonomy are the subject of the earlier observer-measurements page, which is a declared prerequisite of this page; this page consumes its simultaneity and congruence items rather than rebuilding them.

contents.name: Section 7.1 pp. 147-148: accelerated coordinates t = X sinh T, x = X cosh T, proper acceleration 1/X and the diagonals as event horizons
contents.support: The chart domain, the congruence acceleration c^2/rho and the horizon interpretation are stated in clauses (i)-(ii) in the (-+++) convention.

contents.name: Sections 8.1.1-8.1.2 pp. 165-166: no Einstein synchronization in a rotating frame and the synchronization discrepancy accumulating around a closed circuit
contents.support: Clause (iv) states the ring rest-line holonomy exactly and relates it by the factor 2 to the guided-signal return-time difference.

contents.name: Section 8.1.3 p. 166: the Sagnac effect and the ring-laser and fiber-gyroscope applications
contents.support: The exact rational case Omega R = 3c/5 of the theorem's return times and the holonomy factor-2 relation is computed in full.

contents.name: Section 8.1.3 p. 166, Example 1: the Hafele-Keating clock comparison and the Sagnac shift of 210 ns per day
contents.reason: This is an empirical clock-comparison report with measured values and apparatus conditions; empirical content belongs to the experimental-interface page, and this page makes no measurement, uncertainty or statistical claim and imports no numerical outcome.

contents.name: Section 8.1.4 pp. 167-168: the rotating coordinate system and GPS timing
contents.reason: Rotating global coordinate systems and GPS metrology are applications outside the scaffolded guided-ring return-time computation; this page builds no rotating global chart and asserts no navigation or timing precision.

contents.name: Section 9.5.1 pp. 205-206: the definition of a timelike congruence as a family of nonintersecting smooth timelike worldlines filling a region
contents.reason: The congruence definition and its kinematic decomposition are homed on the earlier observer-measurements page as def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics and are consumed here as prerequisites; this page does not re-author them.

contents.name: Section 9.5.2 pp. 206-207: expansion and rigidity, the Bell congruence m/1 with constant diagram spacing and increasing tension, and the Born-rigid ruler
contents.support: The material metric of a congruence, its evolution d/ds G = 2 theta and its constancy under Born rigidity are proved exactly, which is the sharp form of the source's expansion-versus-rigidity discussion.

contents.name: Section 9.5.4 pp. 208-209: the Herglotz-Noether theorem in 1+1 dimensions
contents.reason: The Herglotz-Noether classification is the subject of the earlier observer-measurements page as thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether; this page only uses the translated congruence and the rigidity contrast.

contents.name: Section 9.5.5 pp. 209-211: Bell's spaceship paradox revisited
contents.support: The revisited discussion is absorbed into the thought experiment's clauses (c)-(e), with the rest separation computed through the material metric rather than by the 1+1-dimensional expansion scalar alone.

sources.title: M. Blau, Lecture Notes on General Relativity (University of Bern, last update October 5, 2026, 1052 PDF pages); equations converted from c = 1 to x^0 = c t where used
sources.locator: Section 1.2 items 8-9 pp. 34-36, Section 1.3 pp. 36-40 (constant proper acceleration, Rindler coordinates, lightcones, and the invisible region), and Section 3.4 pp. 90-93 (Rindler coordinates revisited and their ranges); printed page numbers as in the PDF text layer

contents.name: Section 1.2 items 8-9 pp. 34-36: four-velocity normalisation and the four-acceleration orthogonal to the four-velocity
contents.support: The orthogonality and causality used to make sqrt(eta(A,A)) well defined are the content of thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (a)-(b), consumed exactly by this definition.

contents.name: Section 1.3 pp. 36-38: constant proper acceleration, the hyperbolic worldline in the quadrant xi^1 > |xi^0|, and the proper time and acceleration of a rho = const worldline
contents.support: Recomputed with c retained; the flow-line and congruence-acceleration identification is clause (c).

contents.name: Section 1.3 item 2 p. 38: the apparent singular behaviour at rho = 0 is a coordinate singularity
contents.support: The counterexample exhibits the constancy and nondegeneracy of the flat metric in the inertial chart and the chart-domain (rho > 0) origin of the degeneracy.

contents.name: Section 1.3 item 3 pp. 38-39: the Rindler coordinates fail to cover large parts of Minkowski space; an inertial observer crosses eta = +infinity at finite proper time
contents.support: The crossing inertial worldline is the witness of clause (d) of the counterexample.

contents.name: Section 1.3 item 4 pp. 39-40: lightcones in Rindler coordinates and the null equations d eta = +- rho^{-1} d rho
contents.support: The null straight lines of constant U and constant V and their intersection times are computed with these equations inside the proof of clause (iii).

contents.name: Section 1.3 item 5 p. 40: |partial_eta|^2 = (xi^0)^2 - (xi^1)^2 and the lightlike boundary as the locus where the Rindler time-translation generator turns lightlike
contents.support: The boundary identification supports the horizon clause (ii); no Killing-horizon machinery is imported and no gravitational analogy is asserted.

contents.name: Section 1.3 item 6 p. 40: the past lightcone of an accelerated observer asymptotically covers only xi^0 < xi^1, so events above xi^0 = xi^1 are forever invisible; the horizon is observer-dependent
contents.support: The exact causal criterion V(q) < 0 is proved as clause (ii), including the sharp plane case that the source states asymptotically.

contents.name: Section 3.4 pp. 90-93: Rindler coordinates revisited; coordinate ranges -infinity < eta, xi < infinity covering the right quadrant x > |t| and the right Rindler wedge
contents.support: The chart domain and the right-wedge identification are used and restated in clauses (b)-(c).

contents.name: Section 3.4 remarks 1-3 pp. 91-92: time-dependent acceleration, the conformally flat Rindler form and the a -> 0 limit connecting Rindler and Minkowski coordinates
contents.reason: Alternative accelerated coordinate systems and their weak-field or small-acceleration limits are not built on this page; it fixes the single Rindler chart of thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples and uses only its domain and congruence.

contents.name: Section 3.4 remark 4 pp. 92-93: null Rindler coordinates u_R, v_R and the (3+1)-dimensional spherical Rindler generalisation
contents.reason: Only the two-dimensional right-wedge chart is needed for the horizon and radar computations; the null-coordinate and spherical variants are not scaffolded, and their wave-equation applications lie outside this page.

sources.title: D. Giulini, 'Algebraic and geometric structures of Special Relativity', arXiv:math-ph/0602018v2 (survey); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and u^2 = c^2 normalisation converted to eta(n,n) = -1
sources.locator: Section 5.5 'Rigid motion' pp. 41-49 (Definition 7 and equations (121)-(126), the boost-Killing rod example, and the smooth local Herglotz-Noether classification)

contents.name: Section 5.5, Definition 7 and equation (123): Born's definition of rigid motion as L_u h = 0 with h the spatial metric of the normalized flow
contents.support: The lemma uses exactly this rigidity condition (theta = 0) and proves the preservation of the material metric; the h of the item is the same rest metric in the (-+++) convention.

contents.name: Section 5.5, equation (126): L_u h = -Pi_h(L_u g) and the equivalence of rigidity with the projected Killing equation; Killing motions are rigid
contents.reason: The rigidity-versus-Killing equivalence and the Killing converse are homed on the earlier observer-measurements page as def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics (d) and thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether; this page consumes them as prerequisites.

contents.name: Section 5.5 pp. 42-43: the rod in the right wedge generated by the boost Killing field, with flow ct( tau) = x_0 sinh(c tau/x_0), x(tau) = x_0 cosh(c tau/x_0)
contents.support: The same flow is recomputed exactly in the (-+++) convention with c retained, together with its identification as the Rindler congruence flow line.

contents.name: Section 5.5 pp. 43-49: the smooth local Herglotz-Noether classification, including the irrotational affine-plane family with N = 1 + eta(z'', x - z), d sigma(v) = -eta(z',v)/N and acceleration z''/N
contents.reason: The complete smooth local classification is homed on the earlier observer-measurements page as thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether with exactly these data; this page does not rebuild it and makes no global rigidity claim.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Rindler coordinates' (encyclopedia article consulted as a secondary treatment; no count toward the two-treatment requirement)
sources.locator: Sections 'Characteristics of the Rindler frame', 'Variants of transformation formulas', 'The Rindler horizon' and 'Notions of distance'

contents.name: Characteristics of the Rindler frame: the transformation T = x sinh(alpha t), X = x cosh(alpha t), the metric ds^2 = -(alpha x)^2 dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, validity 0 < X < infinity, -X < T < X, and the statement that observers closer to x = 0 accelerate harder
contents.support: The transformation, its domain and the rho-dependence of the acceleration are all present in the lemma and in thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples (b), in the (-+++) convention with c retained.

contents.name: Variants of transformation formulas: Kottler-Moller, Fermi and radar coordinate systems for accelerated observers
contents.reason: The alternative accelerated coordinate systems are not built: this page fixes one Rindler chart on the right wedge and does not develop Fermi coordinates or radar coordinate systems as global constructions.

contents.name: The Rindler horizon: no observer of the congruence can receive signals from events with T >= X nor send signals to events with T <= -X, and the proper acceleration diverges as the horizon is approached
contents.support: The exact if-and-only-if criteria V(q) < 0 and U(q) > 0 and the limits rho -> 0, +infinity are clauses (ii)-(iii).

contents.name: Notions of distance: ruler distance versus radar distance, the null geodesic equation t - t_0 = log(x/x_0), the radar distance x_0 log(1 + h/x_0) and the caution that radar distance need not be symmetric
contents.support: The general radar distance rho_0 |log(rho_m/rho_0)| and the original worked radii 2rho_0 and rho_0/2 are retained. The locally computed additional radius 3rho_0/2 supplies the equal-rest-distance/unequal-radar-distance witness needed for clause (c). No claim is made that the source supplies these exact new event coordinates.

contents.name: History section: Born, Sommerfeld, Kottler, Bollert and Rindler attributions for the border plane and the horizon
contents.reason: Attribution history is not mathematical content and no scaffolded item depends on it; no history remark is built on this page.

contents.name: Unruh radiation and the black-hole near-horizon analogy
contents.reason: The Unruh effect and horizon thermodynamics require quantum fields in accelerated frames; this page is a classical special-relativistic kinematic treatment and excludes quantum effects and gravitation.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Sagnac effect' (encyclopedia article consulted as a secondary treatment; no count toward the two-treatment requirement)
sources.locator: Sections 'Sagnac effect' (basic circular case and formulas) and 'Theory' plus the guided-wave/fiber description and the fringe-displacement paragraph

contents.name: Basic circular case: return times t_1 = 2 pi R/(c - R omega) and t_2 = 2 pi R/(c + R omega), time difference Delta t = 4 pi R^2 omega/(c^2 - R^2 omega^2) and the small-velocity limit 4 A omega/c^2
contents.support: The exact return times and difference are proved in clause (iii) for the adopted ideal guide, and the holonomy comparison is clause (iv).

contents.name: Guided-wave derivation for a nonstretching optical fiber of arbitrary shape, with Delta T = (2/c^2) contour integral of v . dx and independence of the refractive index
contents.reason: This page adopts a single ideal circular guide rotating rigidly with the ring; arbitrary moving-fiber geometry, refractive index, dispersion and absorption are excluded from the model and no optical medium is described.

contents.name: Interference-fringe displacement and phase shift Delta phi = 8 pi omega . A/(lambda c) for a ring interferometer
contents.reason: The interference phase requires a wave-optics model of the guided signals, which this page does not supply; it computes only return times and proper-time differences and makes no phase or interference claim.

contents.name: Sagnac's 1913 experiment and later precision tests of the effect
contents.reason: Empirical reports belong to the experimental-interface page and would require apparatus, sampling and uncertainty analysis; no experiment item is authored here and no measured value is asserted.

contents.name: Modified Sagnac experiments with a moving source or a non-circular light path
contents.reason: Source-motion and path-shape refinements are not part of the adopted rigid-ring ideal-guide model, and their treatment would require the very fiber and phase models this page excludes.
